verses.t: Chi-Yzmachi is the name of the mountain and of their town, where they stayed and settled. And there they tested their greatness and built buildings of lime and stone; the fourth generation of kings and lords did so: Conaché and Belebebqueb, and also Zalel-ahan. And when King Cotuha reigned with Yztayul, as they were called, lords of the throne and the mat, they reigned there in Yzmachi, and made it illustrious and made it a fine town. And there were only three great houses there in Yzmachi; there were not yet the twenty-four great houses. There were only three great houses: a great house of Caviquib, a great house of the Nihaibab and a great house of the Ahan-Quiché; and there were only two great houses of the two branches. And they were all together there in Yzmachi, without wickedness or trouble; there was only peace and quiet, without quarrels or disputes; there was only peace in their hearts, without envy. And their greatness was still small; they had not yet come together in power or in pride. And then they tried to hold it with the shield, there in Yzmachi, as a sign of their reign, and then they made the sign of their empire and of their greatness and majesty. And when the people of Ylocab saw this, they wanted to come and kill Cotuha, and war began because of them; they wanted a king only for themselves. And the people of Ylocab wanted to punish King Yztayul with death; but their envy did not succeed against King Cotuha; rather it came back upon them, the people of Ylocab who were planning to kill the king. And this was the beginning of the revolts and the discords of war. And they came in and took the first town; the soldiers went, and what they wanted was to finish off the Quichés and rule alone; this they desired, and for this they came to seize and take captives. And few were those who escaped and got away. And then the people of Ylocab began to be sacrificed before the god, and this was the payment for their sin against King Cotuha. And many were those who went into slavery and servitude to their captors, and they went to surrender because of the war that was gathering against them; and the town was destroyed and disgraced. The people of Ylocab wanted the empire of the Quiché, but it did not turn out so for them. And this was the beginning of men being sacrificed before the god, when the war was made; and there began the fortifying of the town of Yzmachi, and there greatness began, for great was the empire of the Quiché and of their king. And everywhere there were mighty lords, and no one could break them or attack them; and so they built up the greatness of the kingdom that was founded in Yzmachi. And there the god began to be held in awe, and all the peoples, small and great, feared him; and they saw the slaves going, and that King Cotuha and King Yztayul killed and sacrificed them for their greatness, with those of Nihaibab and those of Ahan-Quiché. And only three tribes or lineages were there in Yzmachi, and there they began to establish the feasts and drinks for their children when they married them. And so those three great houses came together, which were named so by them, and there they drank their drinks and ate their meals, which were the price of the captive daughters. And it was only for the pleasure of their hearts that they ate and drank in their great houses, and this was a sign of thanks and of a banquet, a sign of increase and of their words about the women who would have sons or daughters. And there it was that they grew great, and the seven clans and branches called one another: "We are companions, we of Caviquib, we of Nihaibab and we of Ahan-Quiché." This is what the three clans and the three of the great houses said. And they stayed a long time there in Yzmachi; and having found another town, they left Yzmachi.
